table.title: Government-Secured Foreign Loans Outstanding July 1, 1937
table.caption_extra: Compiled by E. Kann and J. Baylin. Under care of Ministry of Finance. C. = Capital; I. = Interest.

rows: Chinese Imp. Government 4½% Gold Loan of 1898 (Anglo-German)
Redeemable by annual drawings of 0.7202018% for sinking fund. Final payment March 1, 1943.
Chinese Government 5% Reorganization Gold Loan of 1913

Issued in London .. £7,416,680; Paris .. £7,416,660; Berlin .. £6,000,000; Petersburg £2,777,780; Brussels . £1,388,880 — in 5 currencies on the basis of 1 £ = Frs. 25.25 = Mks. 20.45 = Rbls. 9.47 = Y.9.796. Redeemable by 37 annual drawings from 1924 onwards; final redemption July 1, 1960. Secured on Salt Gabelle and Surplus Customs Revenue, subject to existing prior rights. Actually provided for by the Customs revenue, subject to existing prior rights. Nos. 586,668-725,556 of the Russian (yellow) bonds issue have been declared void.
Chinese Republic 5% Gold Loan of 1925 (Banque Industrielle)

Balance of French Boxer Indemnity converted into loan bonds for satisfying claims of Far Eastern creditors of the defunct Banque Industrielle de Chine, and for educational purposes. Final redemption on January 15, 1948. Nos. 532,669-785,000 have the British Bourse Stamp and are counted at the rate of 5 U.S.$ = 1 £.

Balance of converted Belgian Boxer Indemnity. Proceeds of bonds to be devoted to the extent of: 40% to extension and repairs to Lung-Hai Railway, 35% to construction of other railways in China, 25% to educational and charitable purposes. Reduction of capital semi-annually; final payment on January 1, 1941.
Redeemable by semi-annual drawings until January 1, 1947. Secured on British portion of Boxer Indemnity. For completion of Canton-Hankow Railway.
Chinese Imp. Government 5% and 4½% Gold Loan of 1908 (Anglo-French)

Redeemable by annual drawings of £250,000 each. Bearing interest at 5% per annum until October 5, 1923, and thereafter at 4½% until final redemption, which is to take place on October 5, 1938. Secured on Salt revenue up to Tls. 2,350,000 and besides on sundry taxes of the provinces of Chekiang, Kiangsu, Hupeh and Chihli (Hopei).
Chinese Government 5% Gold Loan of 1912 (Crisp Loan)
Redeemable by annual drawings, commencing in 1923 and terminating in September, 1952. In order to bring up arrears it is planned to pay annually from 1935 onward two years' principal instead of one.
Chinese Government 8% Tenth Year £ Treasury Notes of 1919 (Vickers)

According to rearrangement made in October, 1936, secured on salt, subject to prior claims. Redemption to begin June 30, 1941, with 1% for first 3 years; 2% for next 4 years; 2½% for next 8 years; 3% for next 11 years and 4% for final 9 years, ending in 1975. Interest 1½% for year ending July 1, 1937, with annual rates rising by ½%, reaching 3% in 1942-43 and maintaining that rate until the close.
Chinese Government 8% 10-Year Treasury Notes of Aug. 27, 1918 (Marconis)
[Same remark as the preceding loan: one braced remark is printed against both the Vickers and Marconi notes.]
6% Treasury Notes in Jap. Gold Yen for the Compensation of Public Properties and Salt Interests in Tsingtao (1923)
Contracted in Peking on December 1, 1922. Redeemable by half-yearly instalments of Y.500,000 each, ending March 13, 1938. Secured on Salt surplus and Customs surpluses.
Chinese Government 8% Bonds for Refunding Internal and Short-Term Debts (1922)

This is the Japanese portion of the 96 million dollar internal loan of February 11, 1922. Issued with the security of the surplus Salt revenues, and which was redeemable by 13 instalments, beginning January 31, 1923, and ending January 31, 1929.
Republic of China 6% Three Year Secured Gold Loan Treasury Notes of 1921

Readjusted in April, 1937. Interest until November 1, 1939, at 2½% per annum. Thereafter 5% per annum. Redemption beginning 1942 and ending 1954, viz., 1942-43, $275,000; 1944-45, $330,000; 1946-47, $385,000; 1948-49, $440,000; 1950-51, $495,000; 1952-54, $550,000 annually. Secured on Salt revenue, subject to prior claims.
Republic of China Three Year Secured Loan of 1921, 5% (from scrip)
Representing one-fifth of interest in arrears converted into non-interest-bearing scrip. Redeemable like the foregoing main loan.
Chinese Government 5% Gold Loan of 1914 (Pukow Loan)
C. Fr. 9,014,593 from the start; I. Fr. 75,000,000 since 1/3/1922 Coupon 15

Redeemable at par by 35 annual drawings beginning March 1, 1930. Nominally secured on certain industrial undertakings, on certain taxes of the Peking Municipality, and on the alcohol tax North of the Yangtze.
Republic of China 6% Two Year Secured Gold Loan Treasury Notes of 1919
C. $5,500,000 from the start; I. $7,150,000 since June 1, 1920
Issued on December 1, 1919, by the Pacific Development Corp. Secured on Wine and Tobacco Taxes. As from December 1, 1921, interest has been raised to 8% per annum. (Since readjusted.)
Chinese Government 8% Loans of September 30, 1925 (Skoda Loans)
C. £6,866,046; I. £6,316,762 both from the start

Representing the consolidation of all previous Austrian (Skoda) loans made to China between 1912 and 1922. Nominal security a first mortgage on the Peiping octroi revenues, on the title deed tax and other Government income, but invariably defaulted upon. In 1925 another consolidation scheme was turned into effect in terms of which this loan now stands as indicated.
Chinese Government 5% Cotton and Wheat Loan of June, 1933

Originally granted to the extent of $50,000,000 in the shape of cotton, wheat and flour by the Reconstruction Finance Corp. and the Grain Stabilization Corp. for three years, the balance of the obligation was taken over in May, 1936, by the Export & Import Bank. Redeemable $2,000,000 in 1937 and $2,800,000 each in 1938-42, quarterly instalments.
The 26th Year U.S.$ Loan for Engineering Works Harbour Development in Kwangtung, 6% issued April 1, 1937
For developing Whampoa Harbour and the Pearl River, Canton. Redemption semi-annually within 16 years, ending 1953. Secured on a 5% Customs import surtax to be collected in Canton.
